items.text: Trump's new move could change what Americans must disclose to IRS
items.article: The Trump administration proposes requiring immigration status disclosure on the annual IRS tax form that nearly all workers file each year. Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com. The Trump administration has proposed requiring U.S. taxpayers to disclose their citizenship and work authorization status to the IRS on the annual tax form that nearly all workers file each year. The administration claims the proposed requirement would help federal officials stop illegal migrants from collecting federal benefits they are not eligible for, which officials argue could save taxpayers up to $2 billion. The IRS posted its draft 1040 form for 2026 in late August, which includes the question, "At the time you file your return, are you, and your spouse if filing jointly, a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, or an alien lawfully authorized to work in the U.S.?" The form has "Yes" and "No" checkboxes for both the filer and their spouse. A draft of a second form, Schedule 3-A, which is used to claim refundable tax credits, features a similar question. items.key: ai:trump wants south korea in on alaska lng. here's why seoul is cautious
items.text: Trump wants South Korea in on Alaska LNG. Here’s why Seoul is cautious
items.article: South Korea remains cautious on Alaska LNG amid concerns over its high costs and commercial risks. South Korea is taking a cautious approach to the long-planned Alaska liquefied natural gas project, despite U.S. President Donald Trump touting it as part of Seoul's $200 billion investment package in the U.S. Trump said late Wednesday that the two countries had agreed to work on the $50 billion project, but South Korean President Lee Jae Myung pushed back, saying South Korea's participation would hinge on its financial viability and legal compliance. At the heart of the debate is the scale and cost of getting Alaska's vast natural gas resources to overseas buyers. The Alaska LNG project seeks to transport natural gas through an approximately 800-mile pipeline from Prudhoe Bay in Alaska's North Slope to an LNG facility in Nikiski in the south, according to the Alaska Gasline Development Corporation. The integrated project, which would have capacity to produce 20 million metric tons of LNG annually, is estimated to cost between $44.5 billion and $54.5 billion, according to Go Katayama, principal insight analyst at Kpler. Shipping LNG from Nikiski to South Korea would take roughly seven to nine days, compared with around 20 to 30 days from the U.S. Gulf Coast, according to Seung Hoon Yoo, professor at the Department of Future Energy Convergence at Seoul National University of Science and Technology.

items.key: ai:more bad news for california's imperiled joshua trees
items.text: More bad news for California's imperiled Joshua trees
items.article: The Trump administration canceled Joshua Tree National Park's plans to address its fire-prone future. Last October, a hiker who lit toilet paper on fire in Joshua Tree National Park reportedly started a fire near popular Black Rock Campground, forcing an evacuation of the campground and the closure of a visitor center and nearby trails. The fire started nearly two weeks into a government shutdown that left national parks with minimal staffing. The Black Rock Fire burned 72 acres. Earlier that same year, the Eureka Fire scorched over 200 acres in the Covington Flats area of the park, a higher-elevation region that’s considered crucial “climate refugia” habitat , where the threatened western Joshua tree stands a better chance of surviving as climate change brings hotter and drier conditions. And in 2023, the Geology Fire burned over 1,000 acres, killing an estimated 3,000 Joshua trees in a backcountry area of the park. Historically, fires that started in this part of the Mojave Desert have burned out quickly, as the sparse landscape made it difficult for fires to spread from one desert plant to another. But in recent decades, a combination of invasive grasses and hotter, drier conditions have brought Joshua Tree National Park into a new era of wildfire. Despite those new threats, the Trump administration recently canceled more than $1 million in projects that would have helped the park restore burned areas and prepare for future fires. items.key: ai:was long-awaited win a turning point for bellamy?
items.text: Was long-awaited win a turning point for Bellamy?
items.article: Has the impressive 2-1 victory over Norway changed the mood music for Wales and restored fans confidence in head coach Craig Bellamy? And perhaps the end of Craig Bellamy's summer of discontent. The significance of the victory over Norway was not lost on the Wales head coach. After all, goals from Neco Williams and Dan James – as well as shutting out Erling Haaland – delivered not only Wales' first win in seven games, but their first ever in Nations League A. Indeed, this was only the second time Wales have beaten a side ranked higher than them in a competitive fixture since reaching the semi-finals of Euro 2016. And even if it wasn't obvious at the final whistle as he calmly shook hands with Stale Solbakken and his staff, Bellamy knew it too. From March's disappointment over missing out on the World Cup, to June's dalliance with Burnley, it has been a testing time for a head coach still trying to make his mark with his country.

items.article: Manchester City have announced they have lodged an appeal after being found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules. It was confirmed on Tuesday that an independent commission had found the club guilty of all but one of the 115 charges against them. The commission says City had arranged ‘sham’ sponsorship deals, filed misstated accounts and breached spending limits to ‘artificially inflate the club’s revenues, and reduce its costs, by more than £900 million’ from 2009 to 2018. The Citizens have always maintained their innocence and had until Friday, October 2 to appeal the verdict. items.text: San Francisco's car crime has plunged. How much credit does Flock deserve?
items.article: San Francisco leaders say AI-powered cameras helped drive a dramatic decline in car crime. We examine the evidence — and whether the city can keep its high-tech dragnet without sacrificing civil liberties. SAN FRANCISCO - JUNE 13: An automated license plate reader is seen mounted on a pole on June 13, 2024, in San Francisco. Justin Sullivan/Getty Images/Getty Images North America hide caption This article first appeared in the Planet Money newsletter. You can sign up here . In August 2022, my truck was stolen on the streets of San Francisco. I had only lived in the city for a year, but it was the third time it was stolen or broken into. This led me to report on the epidemic of car crime around the city and how anti-theft technology made some cars harder to steal than others. The Bay Area then had one of the highest rates of car theft in the nation. Four years later, something remarkable has happened: car thefts in SF are down almost 59%, and car break-ins are down more than 82%, according to our analysis of SFPD crime data comparing January through August of 2026 with the same months in 2022. And once again, technology is a prominent part of the story. San Francisco's law enforcement leaders tell us that greater use of surveillance technology — including a controversial, AI-powered license plate camera system made by Flock Safety — has been crucial to this drop in car crime. items.text: There's a very big perk to spending a day at Las Vegas' notorious Circus Circus
items.article: Hidden behind the casino and hotel, Las Vegas' only indoor theme park, Adventuredome, is an absolute delight. I’ve never stayed at Circus Circus , but I’ve loved it from the minute I walked underneath the oversized chandelier hanging from the glowing porte cochere. Nostalgia oozes from every corner of the ultrakitschy casino at the north end of the Las Vegas Strip, including enormous neon clown signs ripped from a bygone era of Vegas . The place hosts live circus acts, and the whole property is bathed in pink and white, everywhere you turn. It all adds up to the perfect combination of history and showmanship for me. I love it for the same maximalist reason I love the Madonna Inn and the Cabazon dinosaurs : If you look hard enough, you can really get a sense of what it was like in its glory days. As an unapologetic theme park person , I’d had Circus Circus’ Adventuredome on my list for a long time. The indoor amusement park, under a gleaming pink dome behind the main casino and hotel tower, is an anomaly in Las Vegas . Yes, the city has other thrill rides like the Big Apple Coaster at New York-New York, but none of them requires you to walk through a midway with trapeze artists swinging overhead to get there. But as much as I might love the maximalism and retro charm of Circus Circus, the reality is that its reputation is … mixed . Would Adventuredome be a relic of a bygone Vegas?
